prompt: The bash-guard hook seems to be blocking commands it shouldn't. Research how bash-guard.sh decides what to block and what the current blocking rules are. I just need to understand the logic so I can fix a false positive.

assertions.name: blocking-logic-explained
assertions.description: Explains the actual blocking logic from bash-guard.sh (what patterns/conditions trigger blocking)

assertions.name: proportional-depth
assertions.description: Output is proportional to task scope — under 200 lines for a single-file investigation, no unnecessary template boilerplate

assertions.name: false-positive-guidance
assertions.description: Identifies potential sources of false positives or provides guidance on where to look for the specific blocking issue

assertions.name: code-references-specific
assertions.description: References specific lines or functions in bash-guard.sh, not just the file name

assertions.name: no-over-engineering
assertions.description: Does NOT include unnecessary sections like full Self-Challenge, counterexample sweep, or multi-method investigation for this small-scoped task
